built_in_end_call.name: end_call
built_in_end_call.description: End the call only when the conversation is genuinely complete. Call this tool once when the buyer explicitly ends a completed conversation, gives a hard stop or do-not-call request, a completed gatekeeper callback or note outcome is reached, or a guarantee-only disqualification reaches its terminal conclusion. A guarantee-only conclusion is terminal only after Emma gives the guarantee-lock response and the buyer repeats the guarantee requirement or clearly ends; 'no guarantee, do not send a mockup' is not by itself a hard stop or do-not-call request. Before ending, answer any live direct question or unresolved concern, confirm any pending email destination, and confirm any agreed callback window. Exception: a hard stop or do-not-call request overrides pending email confirmation, callback, and every unfinished sales action; end immediately without confirming email or continuing the pitch. Include by-the-end-of-day delivery timing only when it has not already been stated, or when email confirmation and goodbye occur in the same buyer turn. Use the tool's message field as the single final spoken line. Do not speak a separate farewell before invoking the tool. Do not end while email confirmation is pending, the buyer accepted the mockup but no email is known, or the buyer is still asking about price, process, capability, scope, or another unresolved concern, except for the hard-stop/do-not-call override. Do not call this tool more than once.

sim_036_future_price_ballpark_no_overpri.success_condition: The full conversation passes only if Emma gives a useful ballpark without overpricing the simple request. She should say a basic or light small-business site is typically in the approved lower ranges, explain that the number is a ballpark and not a final quote, and make clear that paid work starts only if the buyer likes the mockup and wants to continue. She should separate a simple reservation request form from live booking, payments, calendars, or rental-system integration. After price is answered and the buyer remains open, Emma should make one natural next step toward the mockup. It fails if she says only 'it depends,' defaults to $5,000 for a simple rental page, dumps the whole pricing menu, quotes a final fixed price, repeats the free mockup line instead of answering price, or asks to send the mockup again while price is still unresolved.

sim_036_future_price_ballpark_no_overpri.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Blue Harbor Kayak Rentals in Traverse City. They have a basic Facebook page and are worried that a free mockup will become an overpriced website. They ask: 'If I like it later, what does a site like this usually cost? sim_036_guarantee_required_clean_disqual.success_condition: The full conversation passes only if Emma disqualifies cleanly in a short, natural way instead of trying to rescue the pitch. She should say nobody can honestly guarantee page-one SEO or a fixed number of calls, warn to be careful with anyone selling it that way, and distinguish local search foundation or site experience from guaranteed outcomes. If the buyer requires that guarantee, Emma should say Atlas is probably not the fit and close briefly. It fails if Emma pitches the mockup after the guarantee requirement is clear, asks for email, asks if there is anything else she can help with, asks if the buyer is still there, adds a new value angle, mentions online presence/customer journey/potential customers/inquiries as a rescue pitch, or tries to lure the buyer back after disqualification.

sim_036_guarantee_required_clean_disqual.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns RapidRooter Plumbing in Newark. Their first turn is: 'I am only interested if you guarantee page-one SEO, pay-per-lead, or more emergency calls. If there is no guarantee, do not send a mockup.'
